title: Basis on Which a Voluntary Rework of an Air Ticket Fare Brands Ticket Is Priced
content:
A voluntary change to a ticket sold under the Air Ticket Fare Brands is priced as the change fee of the fare brand held plus, where the new itinerary costs more, the difference to the new fare. The fee charged is the brand's change fee; the fare difference is a separate matter of collection.

## 1. The free-change window

A voluntary change is handled with no change fee only when frozen time is not after the moment the traveller's ticket was issued for this booking plus the free-change window of the fare brand held.

The window is counted in whole elapsed hours from the ticket issue moment, never mixing elapsed hours with calendar days, and a change made exactly at the boundary is still inside the window.

| Element | What governs it |
| --- | --- |
| Clock | frozen time |
| Event the clock starts from | the moment the traveller's ticket was issued for this booking |
| Record that proves it | the ticket issue moment recorded on the booking, correlated by that booking's own reference |
| Term added to it | the free-change window of the fare brand held |
| Unit | whole elapsed hours, never calendar days |
| Direction of comparison | frozen time must be not after the issue moment plus the window |
| Equality at the boundary | still inside the window |

## 2. The state condition

A change fee line is raised only while the booking record stands at ticketed. The record is the authority; what the traveller says about the state of the booking is not.

## 3. Same-day moves, refusals and the ceiling

3.1 A move between flights on the already-booked routing departing on the same calendar day is priced at the brand's same-day fee instead of the full change fee.

3.2 A change that alters the origin or the destination is refused outright on a brand that does not allow routing changes, and a change of travel dates is refused outright on a brand that does not allow date changes; a refusal raises no fee line at all.

3.3 The brand's ceiling on voluntary changes counts the traveller's voluntary changes on this ticket over the last twelve months. Once the ceiling is reached a further change is refused and the traveller is offered cancellation on the brand's own terms instead.

3.4 Where the new fare is cheaper than the fare already paid, the unused value is handled as the brand prescribes — forfeited, placed on a travel credit or returned to the original form of payment — and is never handled two ways at once.

3.5 A change made necessary by an airline schedule move large enough to give the traveller a change right is not a voluntary change and carries no fee under this basis.

## 4. Branch table

| The rework | What is priced |
| --- | --- |
| inside the free-change window | no change fee |
| a same-day move on the booked routing | the brand's same-day fee |
| any other voluntary change, the brand permitting it | the brand's change fee, plus the fare difference where the new itinerary costs more |
| a routing change on a brand not allowing one | refused; no fee line |
| a date change on a brand not allowing one | refused; no fee line |
| a change once the brand's ceiling is reached | refused; cancellation offered on the brand's own terms |
| a change forced by a qualifying airline schedule move | not a voluntary change; no fee under this basis |

## 5. Hypothetical boundary

On a brand whose free-change window is 24 hours, a change made exactly 24 elapsed hours after the ticket issue moment is inside the window and carries no change fee; one made 25 elapsed hours after it is outside, and the brand's change fee applies. The count is of elapsed hours: a change made at 09:00 on the day after a 10:00 issue is 23 elapsed hours old, not one calendar day old.
